newsitem.title: USA: New US Senate panel chief to look at airwave sales.
newsitem.headline: New US Senate panel chief to look at airwave sales.

text.p: The incoming chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee is expected to focus on proposals for auctioning chunks of the nation's airwaves, including a controversial plan to make broadcasters pay for a valuable part of the TV airwaves.

"We want to examine the issue more closely," said Mark Buse, an aide to Arizona Republican John McCain. McCain was tapped by Republican leaders to be the new commerce panel chief following the election loss Tuesday of the current chairman, Larry Pressler of South Dakota.
McCain has been an ardent advocate of selling the nation's airwaves. "He's a free-market guy," Buse said of McCain.
McCain and former Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole ran into staunch opposition from television broadcasters this year over efforts to auction broadcast licenses for high-precision digital TV.
Buse conceded that the plan has enjoyed only limited support in Congress.
He said McCain also is likely to look at the Federal Communication Commission's role in implementing the new telecommunications law, advanced digital television, TV violence and TV ratings.
Buse said McCain will oversee the commerce panel with a bipartisan spirit. "This is all going to be done in a very equitable and bipartisan manner," Buse said.
